title: Nearest-Target Replication and Minimax Treatment Rules for Two-Endpoint Experiments with Interior Policy Targets
banked_reason: D0.5 terminal:below-floor: exact two-endpoint finite-noise minimax result is sound, but the cold referee graded it subfield with paper_score_ceiling 6.6 below the 7.4 field floor and salvageable=false.
gap_reasons: It does not characterize the actual optimality boundary: outside that sufficient region, neither failure of the proposed allocation nor an alternative minimax allocation is established.

The contribution is further confined to common Gaussian variance, fractional enrollment, two predetermined endpoints, and a common-action upper certificate; integer allocation, support selection, heterogeneous variance, and reduced-game computation are not delivered.

The recorded history says the original support-compression, integer-augmentation, and reduced-game program was narrowed before solving, while this theorem expressly excludes those deliverables; restore a promised deliverable or formally amend/restart the advertised commitment rather than presenting the narrow phase theorem as its fulfillment.

The affirmative non-subsumption positioning still relies on a supervisor-attested Liu extraction: the accessible SSRN abstract advertises closely related Lipschitz welfare, finite-budget allocation, and Gaussian-frontier results, but public theorem text was not inspected.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved an exact finite-noise minimax allocation and decision rule for two fixed endpoints on the sufficient region CD ≤ F(Cr,√(v/N)), including randomized fractional allocations, zero-share faces, and a low-bias extension beyond 2D ≤ r. It did not prove a sharp converse or the originally advertised support-compression, integer-allocation, and reduced-game results, so the cold referee capped the package at subfield. A field-tier revival requires a formally restarted broader architecture, not another framing pass over this result.
tldr: For two fixed experimental endpoints and finitely many interior policy targets coupled by one Lipschitz effect vector, nearest-target replication and a common sign-to-probit rule are globally minimax whenever \(CD\le F(Cr,\sqrt{v/N})\), with exact value \(F(Cr,\sqrt{v/N})\) over arbitrary measurable vector rules and revealed ex ante randomized fractional allocations. The geometric condition \(2D\le r\) is an all-\((C,N,v)\) corollary, not the fixed-noise boundary: in the low-bias regime \(0<Cr<\sqrt{v/N}\sqrt{\pi/2}\), the sufficient region is strictly larger. In dimensionless coordinates \(\kappa=Cr/\sqrt{v/N}\) and \(\rho=D/r\), it is \(\rho\le f(\kappa)/\kappa\), where \(f(\kappa)=\sup_{x\ge0}(x+\kappa)\Phi(-x)\), with elbow \(\kappa=\sqrt{\pi/2}\); the simpler condition \(CD\le c_0\sqrt{v/N}\), \(c_0=\sup_{x\ge0}x\Phi(-x)\), also suffices. The rational configuration \(E=\{0,3\}\), \(P=\{1/5,6/5\}\) with equal weights has \(a=1\), \(r=7/10\), \(D=1/2\), and supplies a strict zero-share witness with \(2D>r\). The scalar decision transition is published substrate; the exact finite-noise replication result is the field-tier contribution.
gap: Published scalar bounded-bias treatment theory determines the decision transition for a fixed Gaussian experiment. The supervisor-attested Liu (2026) extraction determines exact fixed-anchor and anchor-authority problems and gives only a small-noise Gaussian approximation that holds anchor locations fixed and explicitly does not optimize replication across them. None of the verified comparator results determines exact finite-noise replication shares across two fixed spatial endpoints for several policy targets coupled by a common Lipschitz effect vector.
fill: Prove the zero-safe facewise experiment equivalence, the antipodal Bayes lower bound, the one-sign scalar reduction, and the mixed-sign upper certificate, then combine them into the exact nearest-target allocation theorem and investigate the sharp phase boundary.
